Do not modify source, inputs, role instructions, contract, or the local gate. Report permission failures without trying alternate paths or commands.

content.content:
1	---
2	name: check-contract
3	description: Check the repo against grill/CONTRACT.md and report drift attributed to a role. Anyone on the team can run this, repeatedly, during the build.
4	---
5	
6	You are checking whether the code matches what the team agreed. Your report
7	tells the person who runs you **who to go talk to** — findings are grouped
8	by role, never presented as a bare file list.
9	
10	## Step 0 — revision integrity, freshness, and pending agreement
11	
12	- Run `npx grill-with-me contract-status` before checking code. Record its exact
13	  revision ID and freshness: fresh means local source/artifact hashes match;
14	  stale means source hashes changed; unknown means source comparison is
15	  unavailable or integrity/recovery is incomplete. Never compare a room's
16	  packVersion with a contract revision. Offline unknown is unverified freshness,
17	  not confirmed drift. Stop on integrity conflicts or unfinished finalization;
18	  do not produce a clean report against mixed prose/types/history.
19	- Read `.grill-with-me/member.json` if present.
20	- This local receipt also names the role this checkout joined as. Put that role's
21	  findings first in the report: they are the only ones the person running
22	  you can fix without going to find someone.
23	- If local state is absent, do not infer a current role from legacy shared
24	  `grill/.room`, `grill/MY-ROLE.md`, or a teammate's spec. Report all roles evenly.
25	- Read `grill/CONTRACT-HISTORY.jsonl` and `grill/CONTRACT-CHANGES.md`.
26	  The current CONTRACT.md is the current truth;
27	  finalized amendments are already applied there. Pending roles in status must
28	  remain visibly pending even when file hashes are fresh. History is an audit
29	  trail, not a second competing version to silently overlay. For legacy
30	  unrecorded contracts, flag freshness unknown and request explicit adoption;
31	  surface prose/history contradictions for reconciliation rather than guessing.
32	
33	## Step 1 — scope the check
34	
35	Do NOT read the whole repo. Derive the file set from the contract itself:
36	
37	1. Every implementing file named in `## Endpoints`
38	2. Files defining the tables/models named in `## Data model`
39	3. Call sites of contract endpoints — grep for each endpoint path literal
40	   and each `Paths` constant usage
41	4. If `grill/contract.ts` exists, run
42	   `npx grill-with-me contract-typecheck <consuming-tsconfig>` first. This uses
43	   the project's installed compiler and real declared typecheck command, plus
44	   selected-project diagnostics. Choose each leaf config in a solution repo.
45	   No compiler/config means unknown; missing or unused imports mean
46	   unintegrated. Neither is a clean typed check. Never automatically download
47	   TypeScript or compile only the generated file. Use the reported consumers
48	   and concrete diagnostics to scope findings; compare existing baseline errors.
49	   Bound imports do not prove both sides of every endpoint use the contract or
50	   establish runtime behavior. Inspect producer/caller boundaries explicitly.
51	
52	If a contract file does not exist yet in the repo, that is a finding
53	("endpoint agreed but not implemented"), not a reason to search elsewhere.
54	
55	## Step 2 — compare
56	
57	For each contract line, check the implementation:
58	
59	- Field names and shapes in responses vs the contract's response shape
60	- Request parsing vs the contract's request shape
61	- Table/column names vs the data model
62	- Who writes state that another role owns
63	- Error behavior where the contract specifies it
64	
65	Only report what you can evidence with a file and line. If you cannot read
66	enough to be sure, say "unverified", never guess. A clean repo must produce
67	an empty report — do not manufacture findings to seem useful.
68	
69	## Step 3 — write grill/CHECK-REPORT.md
70	
71	```markdown
72	# Contract check — <date>
73	_Against contract revision <ID or unrecorded>; freshness <fresh/stale/unknown>; typed integration <result>. M files in scope._
74	
75	## Pending agreement
76	- <revision ID and roles still pending, or none>
77	
78	## ⚠️ <Role name>
79	- `path/to/file.ts:LINE` — what the code does vs what the contract says.
80	  → Talk to <other role> before changing either side.
81	  Outcome: [ ] fix the code   [ ] contract is wrong → run amend-contract   [ ] accepted, ignore
82	
83	## ✅ <Role name>
84	- No drift detected.
85	
86	## Unverified
87	- <anything you could not check, and why>
88	```
89	
90	Every finding offers the three outcomes above — drift is sometimes the
91	contract's fault, and the fix for that is `amend-contract`, not a code
92	change. If a previous CHECK-REPORT.md exists, carry forward its "accepted"
93	markings and label findings not present last time as **NEW**.
94	
95	Finish by summarizing: how many findings, how many new, and — if any —
96	which single conversation between two people would clear the most items.
